recent.reason: capital floor reached, stopping for good

last.minutes: With only 24 hours remaining in the experiment, the desk is prioritizing capital preservation to avoid the high hurdle rate created by transaction costs and the 31.2% tax on gains. The market regime is neutral and range-bound, making it unlikely that any new position would generate enough profit to offset the 1.2% entry friction and potential slippage. The futures book remains flat after reaching its capital floor, and the spot book will remain in cash to secure its current value for the final tally.

lessons.text: Preserving cash in the final stages of an experiment avoids transaction friction and tax drag, protecting terminal capital from forced recovery trades.
The asymmetry of the 31.2% tax on gains without loss offsets makes short-term trading in a neutral market a negative-expectancy activity once transaction costs are included.
